# Form Abandonment Nudge

## Description

This recipe helps marketers automatically re-engage people who started filling out a form on the website but left without submitting it, nudging them to come back and finish.

## Why this works

It first identifies the right audience by watching for people who interacted with a form but did not submit it within a few days, then creates a visual that matches a friendly, non-urgent tone, and finally combines both into a short email that speaks directly to that audience using the generated image, so the whole sequence moves from audience definition to creative to a ready-to-send message.

## Steps

### Step 1: Create Form Abandoners Segment

Create a segment called "Form Abandoners" for users. Base it on the "Change on" event — the default autotracked event that fires when someone interacts with a form field, no integration needed. Add one group with two conditions: triggered "Change on" within the last 3 days, AND did NOT trigger "Submit on" in that same 3-day window.

### Step 2: Generate Nudge Banner Image

Generate a friendly, low-pressure "still there?" banner image — simple and clean, a small progress-bar or checkmark icon, warm color palette, no urgency red or orange tones.

### Step 3: Generate Nudge Email

Write a short, friendly nudge email for the "{{steps.s1.output}}" segment created in Step 1, using the {{steps.s2.output}}. Remind them they started filling something out, reassure them it only takes a minute to finish, and close with one clear button linking back to where they left off.
